  "title": "DB CoTD: October: A (small) nightmare on Wall Street...",
  "type": "macro",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-06",
  "insights": [
   "October was a rotation out of tech and French risk into energy and core government bonds. Oil's +93.3% YTD gain (Brent) remains the dominant theme in the YTD table, while the Philly semiconductor index is still +51.6% YTD despite the October drop.",
   "Oil led October gains. Brent rose +13.6% and WTI +15.2% in USD terms, taking YTD gains to +93.3% and +81.3%. Brent ended the month at $117.64/bbl, close to its 2026 high.",
   "The oil risk premium kept rising on Houthi attacks, Hormuz disruption, and fears of renewed US strikes on Iran after the midterms. European gas rose +43.6% to \u20ac103.94/MWh, its highest since 2022.",
   "Tech was the biggest drag as doubts about AI capex spread from semiconductors to the wider sector. The Philly semiconductor index fell -15.3% in October and -19% from 6 October to month-end.",
   "The Nasdaq lost -5.3%, its worst month since March 2025. Alphabet's -12.64% post-results day was its worst on record.",
   "The KOSPI (-14.7%) was the weakest of the major indices DB tracks, and the Nikkei fell -5.3%.",
   "Treasuries rebounded sharply. The 10yr yield hit a post-2002 high of 5.31% early in the month, then fell to 4.93%. Treasuries returned +2.3%, their best month of 2026, but remain -0.5% YTD.",
   "Weaker risk sentiment and on-hold decisions from the Fed, ECB and BoJ restored the safe-haven bid in government bonds. Gilts gained +2.6%, while Bunds gained only +0.4% in USD because a weaker euro offset most of the rally.",
   "France was the focus of European stress. The 10yr OAT-Bund spread reached 174bps on 22 October, its widest since November 2011, and the French 10yr yield hit 5.07%.",
   "OATs lost -1.7% and BTPs and EU sovereigns lost -0.5%. The euro fell to 1.1160, its lowest since spring 2025, which hurt USD returns on all euro assets.",
   "EU high yield lost -2.5% and European HY spreads widened +65bps to 370bps. European banks fell -11.7%.",
   "Equities rotated beneath the headlines. The S&P 500 fell -0.9% while the equal-weighted index gained +5.0%. In USD, the DAX rose +0.9% and the STOXX 600 +0.5%, so Europe held up outside France and the periphery.",
   "Losses elsewhere were broad. MSCI EM fell -8.0% and Brazil's Bovespa fell -14.3% after Lula's election win. The Shanghai Composite lost -5.3% (-2.7% YTD).",
   "Gold lost -6.8% and silver -18.7% in October, leaving both among the weakest assets YTD (-10.3% and -31.5%)."

  "insights": [
   "US equities fell Friday: S&P 500 -1.82%, Nasdaq -2.86% (worst session since June), Dow -1.09%. The AI trade was the biggest drag, with semis, memory and neoclouds sharply lower. NVDA and SPCX fared worst among big tech. Equal-weight RSP outpaced the cap-weighted index by about 100 bp.",
   "Treasuries rallied on flight-to-safety buying, with yields down 2-8 bp. Gold fell 3.3% (the table shows -3.65%), its worst day since June, and closed back below $4K. Bitcoin futures lost 5.2% after the Binance hack. WTI crude gained 2.1% on skepticism about a diplomatic offramp in Iran.",
   "Amazon fell after earnings. AWS growth of 39% beat expectations but fell short of elevated buyside expectations. Retail and advertising slowed and missed, and Q4 operating income guidance was below consensus at the midpoint. AWS backlog rose to $578B.",
   "Intel fell 28.6%. Q3 EPS beat but revenue missed. Client Computing revenue fell 5.1% y/y to $8.1B against a $8.95B consensus. Q4 EPS and revenue guidance came in well below the Street.    "The megacap tech and semis selloff raises scrutiny of AI funding ahead of Anthropic's expected November IPO. Alphabet is 22% below its $85B June equity offering price, Intel is 33% below its $23B August offer, and Meta's $25B offering is already more than 2% underwater. Blackstone said Anthropic's $63B chip financing is expected to get a high junk rating after the IPO. Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual contracts on Hyperliquid are down about 25% from the 9-Sep peak.",
   "Binance confirmed $6.3B of funds were impacted in a suspected hack, described as the biggest crypto heist ever. Tether and Circle froze $2.54B in linked assets. Coinbase said it was unaffected.",
   "Renewed US strikes on Iran remain on the table after the midterm elections next Tuesday. Iran's Ghalibaf insists the US must first meet preconditions (end the blockade, unfreeze assets, restart oil sales) before nuclear talks resume. CENTCOM commander Cooper gave Trump an in-person briefing. Qatari negotiators are continuing talks in Tehran.",
   "Post-FOMC Fedspeak stayed firm: Dallas Fed's Logan said two more 25 bp hikes are needed before pausing, and St. Louis Fed's Musalem said another hike may come soon.    "US data was light. Q3 ECI rose 0.8% m/m, in line. October Chicago PMI was 55.3 against 56.0 consensus, with prices paid at their highest since December 2021.",
   "The ECB held rates but a December hike is likely unless growth deteriorates notably, with a pause expected after that. Lagarde said a hike was discussed and stressed upside inflation risk. Lagarde will step down on 7-Feb, with de Cos and Knot the leading candidates.",
   "Eurozone October national inflation diverged. German CPI fell to 2.8% y/y from 3.3% (core 2.1% from 2.4%) on a temporary fuel tax cut. France rose to 3.4% from 3.1%.    "The UK Budget was low-key. The OBR cut 2027 growth to 1.0% from 1.6%, and the gilt reaction was muted. Markets price over a 90% chance of a 25 bp BoE hike next week to 4% and about a 50% chance of a December move, with a 6-3 vote split tipped.    "STOXX 600 Q3 earnings growth is 35.8% y/y among the 43% that have reported (blended 26.3%), against 18.9% expected at the start of the season. Sales are up 11.3%, with an aggregate earnings surprise of +2.85% and a sales surprise of -2.13%. Energy drives most of the headline (+135.7% earnings growth). Ex-energy growth is about 17%. Analysts expect Q4 growth of +30.5%. JPMorgan has 2027 EPS growth slowing to +9.5%.",
   "The BOJ held at 1.25% on an 8-1 vote (Takata dissented for a 25 bp hike).    "Asian equities fell on tech weakness: Nikkei -2.12%, Shanghai -1.44%, Hang Seng +1.46%. Taiwan's Taiex closed at two-month lows near a technical correction.   "insights": [
   "Bloom Energy (BE): Project Jupiter, Oracle's data center in Las Cruces, New Mexico, depends on an air permit from the New Mexico Environment Department. The hearing officer rejected New Energy Economy's Motion to Dismiss on Oct 26, leaving the Dec 7 merits hearing on schedule. An opinion is expected by year-end 2026, though the timeline could extend.",
   "Project Jupiter revised its application: fuel-cell stacks cut to 1,263 from 2,275, stack height raised to 45 ft from 30 ft, in 197 pages of revisions and new modeling. Opponents say more accurate facility data roughly doubled modeled pollutant concentrations. NMED has given no completion date for its technical review of the Oct 16 revised application.",
   "Timing matters for Project Jupiter because a favorable ruling before the new governor takes office would let the current Environmental Improvement Board likely deny any appeal. An opinion in January 2027 or later would let the incoming governor influence the board and NMED leadership, adding uncertainty.",
   "Haaland (D), the likely governor-elect, has committed to a data center moratorium on day one but said she 'can't stop Project Jupiter.' Jefferies is increasingly less concerned about the incoming administration for this project, citing labor support and the nearly complete facility.",
   "The Green Chili natural gas pipeline cannot start substantive work until the air permit clears. The incoming Land Commissioner is expected to open negotiations with Oracle in Q1 2027. FERC approval is expected in December. Jefferies does not see the pipeline as the principal gating item.",
   "Water rights are viewed as legally well-settled and not a material risk. The $165Bn Dona Ana County industrial revenue bonds face a retroactive claw-back threat from Senator Cervantes, which would change project economics but not stop the project.",
   "Oracle approached El Paso Electric for backup power covering about 1/4 of the data center's needs. A materially larger external grid share could conflict with the IRB terms tied to on-site generation and require a new IRB.",
   "New Mexico's 2027 legislative session is expected to favor a guardrail bill over an outright data center moratorium. Whether grandfathering covers in-flight projects like Jupiter is an open question. Project Jupiter would deploy over 2 GW of fuel cells once fully operational.",
   "Enphase (ENPH) and Infineon announced a 900 V monolithic GaN bidirectional switch, being integrated into IQ SST development builds. It allows fewer series-connected modules, a unipolar 800 VDC output and a path to 1,500 VDC, which ENPH believes enables a single-stage SST architecture.",
   "Jefferies calls the NVIDIA/Infineon GaN work incremental validation only, since NVIDIA uses GaN at the high-voltage intermediate bus converter stage, not across the full power architecture. The 900 V devices have not completed production qualification, so commercialization is the main open question.",

  "insights": [
   "U.S. ETF flows (as a ratio of assets) into risk-on equity strategies have slowed while flows into risk-off equities and bonds have accelerated. In October 2026 the bond flows-to-assets ratio was the highest since the start of 2025.",

   "Consumer Staples ETFs lost $1.1B and Telecom ETFs lost $0.4B over three months. Almost all Staples outflows came in the past month, even though the sector returned about 6%, which CFRA reads as investors selling the rally.",
   "Non-tech risk-on ETF flows fell from a 2.9% monthly flows-to-assets ratio in January 2026 to 0.1% in October 2026, the lowest since mid-2025.",

   "Emerging markets ETFs took in $14.3B over three months, the only part of non-tech risk-on still drawing meaningful money.",
